title: Pictures of Phil Tippett’s Movie Work Appear Online
summary:
Pictures and videos showing how special-effects artist Phil Tippett helped make films have appeared on the Internet Archive. News about the collection spread during the week before October 4, 2026. A social media post shared the news on October 1.

Tippett and his team worked on Star Wars, Jurassic Park and RoboCop. He is known for stop-motion animation, which makes models of imaginary creatures seem alive. An artist moves an object a little between photographs. When the photographs play in order, the object seems to move.

The collection seems to come from a folder of CDs. An unnamed fan bought them at a sale after Tippett’s studio in Berkeley, California, closed in August 2026. The buyer said some of the material was not online. They wanted to save its clear, fine detail. They copied the contents and uploaded files from 90 different discs.

The Star Wars pictures show work on the cantina scene in A New Hope. They also show puppets, stop-motion creatures and the film’s small holographic chess figures.

Other files show work on RoboCop and surface details for creatures from Hellboy. There are also computer models from Jurassic Park shown as a network of lines. The collection includes photographs from animator Ray Harryhausen’s 90th birthday, too.

Tippett’s studio has closed, but he has said he is not quite ready to retire.
why_it_matters: The collection lets readers see some of the work behind movie creatures and effects.
